stem.text: Ammonium ions, $\text{NH}_4^{+}$, can enter the xylem of plant roots by two pathways.

items: In the apoplast pathway, ammonium ions move through cell walls until this pathway is blocked by the Casparian strip. Ammonium ions then enter the cytoplasm of root cells.
In the symplast pathway, ammonium ions move through the cytoplasm of root cells.

stem.text: A scientist measured the uptake of ammonium ions into the xylem of *Arabidopsis thaliana*.
The *sgn3* mutant of *A. thaliana* does not have a Casparian strip. In the *sgn3* mutant, ammonium ions can enter the xylem without entering the cytoplasm of root cells.
The bar charts show the scientist's results.

stem.alt: Two bar charts of uptake of NH4+ into xylem in μmol g^-1 h^-1 against plant variety, for low and high concentrations of NH4+, each with non-mutant and sgn3 mutant bars.

A.text: Fewer ammonium ions enter the xylem when they have to move through the cytoplasm of root cells.

B.text: More ammonium ions enter the xylem at low soil concentrations of ammonium ions.

C.text: The Casparian strip acts as a barrier to reduce the movement of ammonium ions into the xylem.

D.text: The loss of the Casparian strip has little effect on the movement of ammonium ions into the xylem.
